raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old Caucasian man presented a rash for 1 month that involved the face, trunk, and upper limbs. He was compliant with arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, new onset stypsis, and mild anorectal pain. He reported his last sexual intercourse about 18 months ago, and he had self-healing genital and palmoplantar lesions more than 1 year ago. He denied any sexual relationship during the last 18 months, including oral sex and protected sexual intercourse, and he had never used illicit drugs. Physical examination showed two ulcerative lesions on the lips, painless bilateral cervical lymph nodes, and hyperkeratosis papules on the face, behind the left ear, on the neck, palms, soles, and scrotum (Fig. 1). A macular rash was in the trunk; erosive lesions were on the glans. Papular lesions were mild itching, and some of them were treated previously with cryotherapy for suspicion of common warts. He was afebrile, and his vital parameters were normal. Exams were all unremarkable but ALT (61, reference < 50 U/L). Treponemal test, rapid plasma reagin (RPR) for syphilis and serology for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) were ordered. Testing for HIV returned positive with a CD4 count of 385 (16.96 %, CD4/ CD8 = 0.3), HIV viral load of 43,400, and negative HIV p24 antigen. Syphilis serology was positive, with an elevated RPR titer of 1:128. A diagnosis of mucocutaneous relapse during untreated late latent syphilis with HIV coinfection was made. Molecular panel for sexually transmitted infection (Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium, Chlamydophila trachomatis) on first-void urine and rectal swab was negative. Screening for opportunistic infections, including tuberculosis (Quantiferon Tb Gold), cryptococcosis (serum antigen), toxoplasmosis (serology), and leishmaniasis (serology and polymerase chain reaction) was unremarkable all but positive Toxoplasma gondii IgG serology.
The patient was treated with three doses of 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin administered 1 per week. Antiretroviral therapy with a bictegravir-based regimen was started concurrently with the first administration. Macular rash of the trunk, glans erosions, anorectal pain, and stypsis disappeared after the first dose of penicillin. The other lesions had a progressive improvement in the next three weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old Caucasian man presented with a 1-month history of a diffuse mucocutaneous rash involving the face, trunk, and upper limbs accompanied by arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, new-onset constipation (stypsis), and mild anorectal pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed a mildly pruritic papular and macular rash over the face, trunk, palms, soles, and genitalia 1 month prior to presentation, some of which had been treated with cryotherapy for suspected common warts. He reported having self-healing genital and palmoplantar lesions more than 1 year earlier after his last sexual intercourse 18 months ago.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of untreated self-resolving genital and palmoplantar lesions >1 year prior; denied sexual activity over the past 18 months and denied illicit drug use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for rash, mild pruritus, arthralgias, myalgias, asthenia, constipation, and mild anorectal pain; negative for fever.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile with normal vital signs. Cutaneous and mucosal exam revealed two ulcerative lesions on the lips, painless bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, hyperkeratotic papules on the face, left retroauricular area, neck, palms, soles, and scrotum, a truncal macular rash, and erosive lesions on the glans penis.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests were unremarkable except mildly elevated ALT (61 U/L; ref <50 U/L). Syphilis serology was strongly positive with RPR titer 1:128 and positive treponemal test; HIV serology was positive with HIV viral load 43,400 copies/mL and negative p24 antigen. Urine and rectal swab PCR panel for Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium, and Chlamydia trachomatis was negative; QuantiFERON-TB Gold, serum cryptococcal antigen, and Leishmania serology and PCR were negative; Toxoplasma gondii IgG was positive.
objective.advanced_workup: T-lymphocyte subset analysis showed a CD4 count of 385 cells/uL (16.96%, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.3).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Leishmaniasis, tuberculosis, cryptococcosis, and mucosal STI co-infections were ruled out by negative PCR and antigen/serology panels, establishing a diagnosis of mucocutaneous relapse of untreated late latent syphilis with newly diagnosed HIV co-infection. Treatment with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units weekly for 3 weeks) and concurrent initiation of bictegravir-based antiretroviral therapy resulted in clearance of the truncal rash, glans erosions, anorectal pain, and constipation after the first dose and progressive resolution of the remaining lesions over 3 weeks.
